- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1-2 days); cap forecast at +3–4% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is flat or neutral (0.0–0.3) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply mild downward bias for 5–7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out extremes by averaging last 5–7 days’ sentiment-weighted price.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.6 → -0.4 → +0.6), model often misreads momentum; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for each reversal cycle.
- When sentiment is high but price is stagnant, model overestimates upside; apply downward correction of 0.5–1.5% to avoid “sentiment trap” bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 10–15% below recent 5-day high.
